subject: Business
title: What Is a Supply Chain?
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Is a Supply Chain?.

hook.text: Your morning coffee traveled 6,000 miles — from an Ethiopian farm to your cup. The journey is the supply chain.

buildup.text: A supply chain is every step from raw materials to the finished product in a customer's hands.

discovery.text: It includes suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and all the transport connecting them.

twist.text: Most consumers never see the supply chain. But when it breaks — empty shelves, delayed deliveries — everyone notices.

climax.text: COVID exposed how fragile global supply chains are. One factory shutdown in China emptied stores worldwide.

punchline.text: You don't think about the supply chain until it stops working.

quiz.question: What does a supply chain include?
options: Every step from raw materials to the finished product reaching the customer
Only the transportation between warehouse and store

details.summary: A supply chain is the end-to-end network of organizations, people, activities, and resources involved in creating and delivering a product from raw materials to the final customer. It encompasses sourcing, manufacturing, transportation, warehousing, and retail.
details.whyItMatters: Every product you use traveled a supply chain to reach you. Understanding supply chains reveals how global commerce works and why disruptions at any link can cascade into shortages and price spikes worldwide.
takeaways: Supply chains link raw material extraction through delivery to end customers
Each node adds value through transformation, movement, or storage
Disruption at any point ripples through the entire network

faq.question: What is the difference between a supply chain and logistics?
faq.answer: Logistics is one component of the supply chain focused on transporting and storing goods. A supply chain encompasses the entire process from raw material sourcing through manufacturing, distribution, and delivery to the customer, including information and financial flows.

faq.question: Why are modern supply chains so complex?
faq.answer: Globalization means a single product may source materials from dozens of countries, be assembled in another, and sold worldwide. Specialization, cost optimization, and regulatory requirements add layers of suppliers, intermediaries, and logistics providers.
